extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate / beginning graduate students and researchers in algebraic topology
extracted.subtask_description: Textbook exposition of singular, simplicial, and cellular cohomology: long exact sequences, axioms, excision, Mayer–Vietoris, cup product and cohomology ring, and basic tensor/cross-product preliminaries. Aimed at learning/teaching/proving standard results and computations in cohomology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long exact sequence of cohomology for a pair
rubrics_metrics.description: For a pair (X,A) there is a long exact sequence ... → H^n(X,A;G) → H^n(X;G) → H^n(A;G) → δ → H^{n+1}(X,A;G) → ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arises from a short exact sequence of cochain complexes; connecting homomorphism δ defined by extending cocycles and composing with ∂. Naturality: maps of pairs induce maps between long exact sequences with commuting squares.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long exact sequence for a triple
rubrics_metrics.description: For a triple (X,A,B) there is a long exact sequence coming from the short exact sequences 0 ← C^n(A,B;G) ← C^n(X,B;G) ← C^n(X,A;G) ← 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The long exact sequence of reduced cohomology is the special case when B is a point. The construction is the dual of the corresponding homology short exact sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duality of connecting homomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a duality relation between the connecting homomorphisms δ : H^n(A;G) → H^{n+1}(X,A;G) and ∂ : H_{n+1}(X,A) → H_n(A) taking the form h δ = ∂^* h (commutative square).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verified by representing classes by cocycles, extending to X, composing with boundary maps, and comparing the resulting cochains — the square commutes because both sides are represented by the same cochain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Induced homomorphisms and contravariance
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuous map f : X→Y induces cochain maps f^♯ : C^n(Y;G) → C^n(X;G) and hence homomorphisms f^* : H^n(Y;G) → H^n(X;G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The relation f^♯ ∂ = ∂ f^♯ dualizes to δ f^♯ = f^♯ δ, giving (f∘g)^* = g^* ∘ f^*. Thus X ↦ H^n(X;G) and (X,A) ↦ H^n(X,A;G) are contravariant functors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algebraic universal coefficient theorem (naturality, relative form)
rubrics_metrics.description: The algebraic universal coefficient theorem applies to relative cohomology since relative chain groups C_n(X,A) are free; maps of pairs induce commutative diagrams between the algebraic universal coefficient sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Naturality follows because vertical maps are induced by chain maps f_♯ : C_n(X,A) → C_n(Y,B). Setting A or B empty recovers absolute forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homotopy invariance of cohomology
rubrics_metrics.description: If f ≃ g : (X,A) → (Y,B) then f^* = g^* : H^n(Y,B) → H^n(X,A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by dualizing the homology chain homotopy: a chain homotopy P with g_♯ − f_♯ = ∂P + P∂ dualizes to a chain homotopy between f^♯ and g^♯, hence they induce the same map on cohomology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excision for cohomology
rubrics_metrics.description: If Z ⊂ A ⊂ X with closure(Z) contained in interior(A), then inclusion i : (X − Z, A − Z) → (X,A) induces isomorphisms i^* : H^n(X,A;G) → H^n(X − Z, A − Z;G) for all n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from excision for homology together with naturality of the universal coefficient theorem and the five-lemma, or by dualizing the homology proof using Hom(−,G) and chain homotopies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Axioms for (reduced) cohomology theories
rubrics_metrics.description: A reduced cohomology theory on CW complexes is a sequence of functors h^n together with natural coboundary homomorphisms δ : h^n(A) → h^{n+1}(X/A) satisfying (1) homotopy invariance, (2) long exact sequence for a pair, and (3) wedge sum axiom: h^n(∨_α X_α) ≈ ∏_α h^n(X_α).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The wedge axiom involves direct product (not direct sum) because cochains on a disjoint union are direct products of individual cochain complexes; axioms for singular cohomology are verified via excision and the universal coefficient isomorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality of simplicial and singular cohomology for complexes
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a simplicial complex and A ⊂ X a subcomplex, then simplicial cochain groups Hom(Δ_n(X,A),G) give cohomology H^n(X,A;G) and the canonical maps induce isomorphisms H^n_simplicial(X,A;G) ≈ H^n_singular(X,A;G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The dual maps from inclusion induce isomorphisms on cohomology by Corollary 3.4 and naturality of the dualization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cellular cohomology theorem
rubrics_metrics.description: For a CW complex X with cellular coboundary maps d_n the cellular cohomology groups satisfy H^n(X;G) ≈ Ker d_n / Im d_{n-1}, and the cellular cochain complex is isomorphic to the dual of the cellular chain complex obtained by applying Hom(−,G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses the universal coefficient theorem to show vanishing in certain degrees and long exact sequences of pairs; naturality of h and commutativity of diagrams identify the compositions giving the coboundary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mayer–Vietoris sequence for cohomology (absolute and relative)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is the union of interiors of A and B, there is a long exact Mayer–Vietoris sequence ... → H^n(X;G) → H^n(A;G) ⊕ H^n(B;G) → H^n(A∩B;G) → H^{n+1}(X;G) → ... and a relative version for pairs (X,Y) = (A∪B, C∪D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived from the short exact sequence of cochain complexes 0 → C^n(A+B;G) → C^n(A;G) ⊕ C^n(B;G) → C^n(A∩B;G) → 0, with maps given by restrictions and differences; relative MV uses analogous short exact sequence and five-lemma arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of cup product (cochain level)
rubrics_metrics.description: For cochains ϕ ∈ C^k(X;R) and ψ ∈ C^ℓ(X;R) define (ϕ ∪ ψ)(σ) = ϕ(σ|[v_0,...,v_k]) · ψ(σ|[v_k,...,v_{k+ℓ}]) where the right-hand side is the product in R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This elementary simplicial/singular formula induces a product on cohomology because of the coboundary relation (Leibniz rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Leibniz rule for δ and cup product
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma 3.6: δ(ϕ ∪ ψ) = δϕ ∪ ψ + (−1)^k ϕ ∪ δψ for ϕ ∈ C^k, ψ ∈ C^ℓ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences: cup product of two cocycles is a cocycle; cup product of a cocycle with a coboundary (either order) is a coboundary. Hence cup product descends to cohomology H^k × H^ℓ → H^{k+ℓ}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic algebraic properties of cup product
rubrics_metrics.description: Cup product is associative and distributive; if R has an identity then 1 ∈ H^0(X;R) is an identity for cup product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These properties hold at the cochain level and pass to cohomology. Simplicial and singular cup products are compatible via canonical isomorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative and mixed cup products
rubrics_metrics.description: There are induced cup products H^k(X;R) × H^ℓ(X,A;R) → H^{k+ℓ}(X,A;R), H^k(X,A;R) × H^ℓ(X;R) → H^{k+ℓ}(X,A;R), H^k(X,A;R) × H^ℓ(X,A;R) → H^{k+ℓ}(X,A;R), and more generally H^k(X,A;R) × H^ℓ(X,B;R) → H^{k+ℓ}(X,A∪B;R) when A,B are open or subcomplexes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructed by restricting absolute cup product to cochains vanishing on A or B; uses isomorphisms C^n(X,A∪B;R) → C^n(X,A+B;R) induced on cohomology (excision/five-lemma).

rubrics_metrics.name: Functoriality of cup product under maps
rubrics_metrics.description: For a map f : X → Y, the induced maps satisfy f^*(α ∪ β) = f^*(α) ∪ f^*(β), and similarly in the relative case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from the cochain formula f^♯(ϕ) ∪ f^♯(ψ) = f^♯(ϕ ∪ ψ) because pullback commutes with restriction of simplices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graded commutativity of cup product
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem 3.11: For commutative R, α ∪ β = (−1)^{kℓ} β ∪ α for α∈H^k(X,A;R) and β∈H^ℓ(X,A;R).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses a vertex-reversal chain map ρ (with sign ε_n) that is chain homotopic to the identity; consequence: if k is odd then 2(α ∪ α) = 0, so α^2 may vanish when H^{2k} has no 2-torsion. The theorem applies equally in relative cohomology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohomology ring (graded algebra) structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Define H^*(X;R) = ⊕_{n≥0} H^n(X;R) with multiplication given by cup product; this makes H^*(X;R) into a graded ring (and R-algebra) with grading H^k × H^ℓ → H^{k+ℓ}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One regards H^*(X;R) as a graded ring; the ring is graded-commutative per Theorem 3.11. Examples: H^*(RP^2;Z_2) ≈ Z_2[α]/(α^3), exterior algebras for tori, polynomial/truncated polynomial rings for projective spaces. Ring structure can distinguish spaces not separated by additive cohomology alone (e.g., CP^2 vs S^2 ∨ S^4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Realization problem for cohomology algebras
rubrics_metrics.description: Which graded commutative R-algebras occur as cup product algebras H^*(X;R) of spaces X?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Difficulty depends on R: R = Q essentially every graded commutative Q-algebra is realizable (Quillen 1969), R = Z_p is much harder with partial results, R = Z is hardest and less is known beyond consequences of the Z_p cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross product and relation to tensor products (Künneth direction)
rubrics_metrics.description: The cross product (external cup product) × : H^*(X;R) × H^*(Y;R) → H^*(X×Y;R) is given by a×b = p_1^*(a) ∪ p_2^*(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because a bilinear map is not generally an isomorphism, replace H^*(X)×H^*(Y) by the tensor product H^*(X) ⊗_R H^*(Y). The text reviews tensor product basics (properties 1–7) to prepare for the Künneth formula and algebraic descriptions of H^*(X×Y;R).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensor product elementary properties relevant to cohomology
rubrics_metrics.description: List of elementary tensor-product facts used later: A⊗B ≈ B⊗A; (⊕_i A_i)⊗B ≈ ⊕_i (A_i⊗B); associativity; Z⊗A ≈ A; Z_n⊗A ≈ A/nA; and functoriality (f⊗g)(a⊗b) = f(a)⊗g(b); bilinear maps induce homomorphisms from the tensor product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These properties allow calculation of tensor products of finitely generated abelian groups and underlie the algebraic Künneth-type statements for cohomology rings.
